title: AI pixel tools discussion: PixelLab vs Spritefusion vs Claude-Pxl skill vs (?)
author: delusion54
selftext:
Hello fellow aidev explorers, and especially pixel art oriented ones. Those of you that have tried these tools, or more that I haven't heard of, what has been your experience with them?  
  
I have mainly spent dozens of hours with a custom skill I tweaked, then transitioned to the [https://github.com/crsolver/claude-pxl](https://github.com/crsolver/claude-pxl) skill and ended up subscribing to PixelLab which generally has been an improvement but not absolutely a leap. I have no experience with spritefusion yet.

Glad to hear your experiences and reviews.

comments.author: Any_Candle_6953
comments.body:
My process and what has worked for me so far:

I have used ChatGPT to generate a single pixel image based on an already existing "concept art" piece that I have given it.

Then, I have taken that pixel art and uploaded it to autosprite, and had autosprite make spritesheets for me.

comments.author: KeldornWithCarsomyr
comments.body:
Sol5.1 to make and tweak the original, pixel labs to make a sprite to be animated. Astra to touch it up. Pixel labs to animate and then astra touches up all the animated sprites in aseprite then manual frame by frame review.

Unfortunately this only works for the one specific style "world map". Finding it to be a lot more work when creating unique animation.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
I have tried Pixel Lab and Sprite Fusion extensively. 

They are both tools that are... frustratingly competent. I want to like them. 

  
I think the creators of those tools have done the best they can with the technology in it's current state, and for some projects the tools will work fine. 

  
Here are my gripes with both tools (they both have the same fundamental problems): 

 \- The colors are too flat. I suspect that you ultimately MUST train the model to do flat colors in order to get crisp results, but the result is images with the opposite problem to the noise issue that plagues normal AI generator mixel art: they are so flat that nothing pops. At best, this results in characters that look boring; at worst, it means you have to generate absolutely everything in those generators because it looks weird to put a flat character into a shaded pixel environment. And if you generate your environment and VFX in those tools, the flat colors make everything blend together too much.

 \- Poses are incredibly boring. There is just no emotion, no mystoire, no flourish to a character made in Sprite Fusion or Pixel Lab. It's the same problem Nano Banana has (or did have, when it had a fidelity advantage): the accuracy (and Pixel Lab and Sprite Fusion are INCREDIBLY accurate; it's amazing how good they are at following a prompt) comes at the cost of rigid variation. 

 \- Cost is just too comparably high. I know for a fact that the guys running these models are not making money doing it; that the only reason GPT or Claude is so cheap by comparison is that we're currently being subsidized. But... well, wer're being subsidized, and these platforms can't afford to subsidize their users. When my options are to generate mixel art with an interesting pose and grid snap it and then clean it up and just using a smoothing option to get rid of the noise, at no extra cost to my coding plan, or alternatively create a clean and accurate pixel perfect sprite with completely flat colors and no emotion... I mean, for me that's not a contest. I go with the mixels. 

Here is my ideal sprite in terms of quality and overall vibe (this is the basic wolf sprite from Songs of Conquest):  


https://i.redd.it/u7w2j5mkh5zh1.png

  
Personally, I don't need animations or anything super fancy. I need good hue shifting, good accuracy, and a character that looks like they have something going on in their head. 

Pixel Lab and Sprite Fusion delivers 1 of 3 of those things right now, albeit with a very clean end result and interesting animation tools. 

At the current price point, 1 of 3 of my needs isn't good enough.
